accueil_bienvenue: Welcome to JÀMMU XEL. Touch the speaker to hear each language, then choose yours.
qui_joue: Who is playing? A child, or an adult who wants to understand?
maintenir_quitter: Keep your finger pressed to leave.
j_consigne: Put the day in order. What comes first?
r_intro: The leaf opens when you breathe in. It closes when you breathe out. Stay as long as you like.
penc_intro: This is the Pénc. Touch a path to walk alongside someone.
lieu_ressources: The resource house. Recognize the signs and know where to get help.
carnet_vide: Your notebook is empty. Walk with Awa to fill it.
carnet_avertissement: This notebook is not a diagnosis. Only a professional can assess a child.
carnet_local: Nothing is sent over the Internet. The notebook stays on this phone.
obs_voitures: He lines up his toys for a long time, always in the same order.
obs_prenom: He rarely responds when called by his name.
obs_bruit: He covers his ears when it is noisy.
obs_mots: He says few words for his age.
trouver_structure: Find a care centre near me
trouver_structure_voix: I am opening the SAMA XHEL directory of mental health centres.
awa_intro: Walk with Awa and her son Amadou. Observe, listen, and help them take the first step.
a1: Amadou is three. He lines up his little cars for hours. When I call him, he doesn't turn around. What do you see?
a1_c1: I write down what I see, without giving it a name.
a1_c2: I ask Awa how she feels.
a1_c3: I tell her it will pass on its own.
a1_r1: Good idea. We write down facts: he lines up his toys, he rarely answers to his name. These are observations, not a diagnosis.
a1_r2: Thank you for asking. I am worried, and I feel a little alone.
a1_r3: Many people say that. But waiting loses time: the earlier we consult, the more we can help the child.
a2: At the market, Amadou covers his ears and cries. The noise is too loud for him.
a2_c1: I take him to a quieter spot.
a2_c2: I tell him to stop being difficult.
a2_c3: I write down: he is bothered by noise.
a2_r1: He calms down. Some children feel noises, lights or textures much more strongly than we do.
a2_r2: He isn't doing it on purpose: for him, the noise really hurts. Scolding him doesn't help.
a2_r3: Noted. This observation will help the professional.
a3: This child has the evil eye. He must be taken to a healer, not to the hospital.
a3_c1: I answer respectfully: a health professional can assess him.
a3_c2: I make fun of the neighbour.
a3_r1: The neighbour listens. We can respect beliefs and still consult a health professional.
a3_r2: Mocking ends the conversation. It is better to explain gently.
a3_r3: Silence leaves Awa alone with the misconceptions. A calm word can help her.
a4: I don't know what to tell the doctor.
a4_c2: Just tell him the child is strange.
a4_r1: Here it is: precise facts, since when, and our questions. The notebook is ready.
a4_r2: The word “strange” doesn't help. Describing what we see helps much more.
a5: Thank you for these very clear observations. We will assess Amadou's development. Only a professional can say whether it is autism.
a5_c1: How can we help him at home in the meantime?
a5_r1: Speak to him in short sentences, show pictures, keep routines, and warn him before a change.
a6: Amadou plays at the Pénc with the other children, with his cars. Everyone has a place.
awa_bilan: What you learned: observe without judging, understand sensitivity to noise, answer misconceptions respectfully, prepare the appointment and consult early.
modou_intro: Walk with Modou, a high-school student who is not doing well.
m1: For weeks I haven't felt like doing anything. I sleep badly, I don't go to football anymore. Ibou wrote to me three times. I didn't answer.
m1_c1: Answer Ibou, even with one word.
m1_c2: Open the window and go out for a while.
m1_c3: Think of a trusted adult to talk to.
m1_r1: Ibou replies right away: “I'm glad to hear from you.”
m1_r2: The fresh air helps. It isn't a solution, but it is a small step.
m1_r3: Modou thinks of his aunt. Talking to someone you trust is a real first step.
modou_bilan: Sadness or loss of interest lasting more than two weeks, with tiredness or sleep problems, can be depression. It is not a lack of effort. Talk to a trusted adult and see a professional.
urgence: If someone talks about dying or hurting themselves, do not leave them alone and get help right away.
maam_intro: Walk with Grandma Coumba and her granddaughter Ndèye.
k1: Grandma Coumba forgets where she puts her things. Yesterday she got lost coming back from the market.
k1_c1: Shout at her so she pays attention.
k1_c2: Put photos and signs around the house.
k1_c3: Make an appointment with a doctor.
k1_r1: Shouting frightens her and makes her sad. She doesn't forget on purpose.
k1_r2: The signs help her stay independent. Grandma Coumba smiles.
k1_r3: Good idea. The doctor can look for the cause: some causes can be treated.
maam_bilan: Forgetting now and then is normal. But getting lost in a familiar place, forgetting recent events or struggling with daily tasks should lead to a consultation. Always respect the person's dignity.
signes_avert: This information helps you recognize signs. It does not replace a professional and gives no diagnosis.
s_autisme_s: In young children: little eye contact or shared smiles, few words, rarely answering to their name, repetitive play, strong distress with noise or change.
s_autisme_c: Consult as soon as these signs worry you: early detection helps the child.
s_tdah_s: A child who cannot sit still, cannot concentrate and acts without thinking, at home and at school, for several months.
s_tdah_c: Consult if it affects school or home life. It is not a lack of upbringing.
s_depression_s: Sadness or loss of interest almost every day for more than two weeks, with tiredness, sleep or appetite problems, difficulty concentrating, feeling worthless.
s_depression_c: See a professional. If someone talks about dying or hurting themselves, do not leave them alone and get help right away.
s_memoire_s: Forgetting recent events, getting lost in a familiar place, repeating the same questions, struggling with everyday tasks, mood changes.
s_memoire_c: See a doctor: some causes can be treated. Always respect the person's dignity.
s_addiction_s: No longer being able to stop using a drug, alcohol, tobacco or gambling, thinking about it all the time, continuing despite problems, feeling bad when stopping.
s_addiction_c: Addiction can be treated. Specialised centres support people without judging them.
xel_intro: I am Xel. Ask me a question, or touch a question below. I do not make diagnoses.
xel_inconnu: I don't know the answer yet. Talk to a health professional, or touch “Find a care centre”.
xq_autiste: How can I tell if my child is autistic?
xa_autiste: Some signs should lead you to consult: little shared eye contact, few words, rarely answering to their name, repetitive play, strong distress with noise. Only a professional can say whether it is autism.
xq_cause: Is autism caused by the evil eye or by the parents?
xa_cause: No. Autism is nobody's fault, neither the parents' nor a spell's. It is a difference in how the brain develops. The child needs support.
xa_guerir: Autism is not cured like an illness, but early support greatly helps the child to communicate and become more independent.
xq_parle: My child is not talking yet, what should I do?
xa_parle: If your child speaks little for their age, talk to a health professional. Meanwhile, speak in short sentences and show pictures. The “I speak” game can help them be understood.
xq_ou: Where can I get help in Senegal?
xa_ou: Touch “Find a care centre”: the SAMA XHEL directory lists the country's hospitals and mental health centres.
xq_mourir: Someone talks about dying, what should I do?
xa_mourir: Take it seriously. Do not leave them alone, listen without judging, remove anything that could hurt them and get help right away from a professional or an emergency service.
xq_memoire: My grandmother forgets a lot, is it normal?
xq_tdah: My child cannot sit still, what should I do?
xq_drogue: How can I help someone who uses drugs?
xa_drogue: Talk to them calmly, without humiliating them. Addiction is an illness that can be treated. Suggest they visit a specialised centre.
xq_crise: My child has meltdowns, what should I do?
xa_crise: Stay calm, speak softly, move away from noise and crowds, protect the child without forcing. Note what triggered the meltdown to tell the professional.
xq_ecole: Can an autistic child go to school?
xa_ecole: Yes. With adjustments and support, many autistic children learn at school. There are also specialised schools and centres: ask a professional for advice.
xq_tradi: Can we see a traditional healer and a doctor?
xa_tradi: Every family makes its own choices. What matters is not to delay seeing a health professional, especially for a child.
xa_jeu: This game helps you understand mental health, recognize signs and know where to get help. It makes no diagnosis.
xq_donnees: Does the game keep my information?
xa_donnees: No. Nothing is sent over the Internet. The notebook stays on this phone and you can erase it.
